content: The drug combination nirmatrelvir/ritonavir interacts with various medications by altering their metabolism, primarily through the inhibition of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Below are the specific interactions and recommendations for coadministration: 1. Isavuconazonium sulfate: Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases its levels or effects. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 2. Ivosidenib: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or consider an alternative drug due to the risk of serious adverse events, such as QT interval prolongation. 3. Leniolisib: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 4. Lurbinectedin: Levels or effects are increased. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lurbinectedin dose by 50%. After discontinuing the strong CYP3A inhibitor for 5 half-lives, resume the original dose. 5. Neratinib: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 6. Nilotinib: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the nilotinib dose. 7. Nirogacestat: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Omaveloxolone: Levels or effects are increased. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects occur. 9. Palovarotene: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 10. Pirtobrutinib: Levels or effects are increased. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the dose by 50 mg. If the current dose is 50 mg daily, discontinue pirtobrutinib during the use of the strong CYP3A inhibitor. Resume the original dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 11. Repotrectinib: Levels or effects are increased via CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 12. Rifapentine: Decreases the levels or effects of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 13. Rimegepant: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 14. Rivaroxaban: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitors due to an increased bleeding risk. 15. Salmeterol: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration due to an increased risk of cardiovascular adverse events, including QT prolongation, palpitations, and sinus tachycardia. 16. Sirolimus: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 17. Sparsentan: Both drugs may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid coadministration. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration upon resumption. 18. Suvorexant: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 19. Tacrolimus: Levels or effects are increased. If unavoidable, decrease the tacrolimus dose by one-third. Monitor for serious adverse reactions, such as neurotoxicity and QT prolongation. 20. Tadalafil: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration if tadalafil is used for pulmonary arterial hypertension. Reduce the dose if used for erectile dysfunction. 21. Tamsulosin: Levels or effects are increased. Pause tamsulosin and restart 3 days after completing nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 22. Ticagrelor: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration. Consider prasugrel as an alternative antiplatelet agent unless contraindicated. 23. Venetoclax: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 24. Vorapaxar: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Voriconazole: Levels or effects are decreased. Avoid coadministration with low-dose ritonavir (100 mg every 12 hours) due to CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 induction. 26. Abemaciclib: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dose if coadministered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 27. Alprazolam: Levels or effects are increased. Consider lowering the alprazolam dose during coadministration. 28. Amlodipine: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dose by 50% during coadministration and for 3 days after the last nirmatrelvir/ritonavir dose. 29. Atazanavir: Levels or effects are increased. Use caution and monitor for adverse events. 30. Atorvastatin: Levels or effects are increased. Consider temporarily discontinuing atorvastatin during nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 31. Bedaquiline: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for adverse effects, such as QT prolongation. 32. Betamethasone: Levels or effects are increased. Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids like beclomethasone or prednisolone. 33. Bictegravir: Levels or effects are increased. 34. Budesonide: Levels or effects are increased. Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids. 35. Bupropion: Levels or effects are decreased. Monitor for adequate clinical response. 36. Ceritinib: Levels or effects are increased. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 37. Ciclesonide (inhaled): Levels or effects are increased. Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids. 38. Clarithromycin: Levels or effects are increased. Do not exceed doses >1,000 mg/day. Consider dose reduction in patients with renal impairment. 39. Dabigatran: Levels or effects are increased via P-gp inhibition. Dose adjustment may be necessary in patients with mild/moderate renal impairment. Avoid in severe renal impairment. 40. Darunavir: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for adverse events. 41. Dasatinib: Levels or effects are increased. Dose reduction may be necessary. 42. Dexamethasone: Levels or effects are increased. Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids. 43. Digoxin: Levels or effects are increased via P-gp inhibition. Reduce the dose by 30-50% or modify dosing frequency. 44. Diltiazem: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dose by 50% during coadministration and for 3 days after the last dose. 45. Doxazosin: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for bradycardia, hypotension, or dizziness. Temporarily pause the antihypertensive drug if needed. 46. Edoxaban: Levels or effects are increased via P-gp inhibition. Consider temporary dose reduction or switching to low molecular weight heparin (LMWH). 47. Efavirenz: Levels or effects are increased. Use caution and monitor. 48. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate): Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for adverse effects, including QT prolongation. 49. Ethinyl estradiol: Levels or effects are decreased. Use additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods for the remainder of the cycle. 50. Felodipine: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dose by 50% during coadministration and for 3 days after the last dose. 51. Fentanyl: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for therapeutic and adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Reduce the dose if necessary. 52. Fluticasone (furoate and inhaled): Levels or effects are increased. Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids. 53. Fosamprenavir: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for adverse events. 54. Hydrocodone: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for therapeutic and adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Reduce the dose if necessary. 55. Indinavir: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for adverse events. 56. Itraconazole: Levels or effects are increased. Limit the adult dose to 200 mg/day. 57. Ivacaftor: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dosage of ivacaftor or combination therapies (e.g., elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor). 58. Ketoconazole: Levels or effects are increased. Limit the adult dose to 200 mg/day. 59. Labetalol: Levels or effects are decreased due to UGT2B7 induction. No dosage modification is needed due to the short duration of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 60. Lenacapavir: Levels or effects are increased. Use caution and monitor for adverse reactions. 61. Levo-ketoconazole: Levels or effects are increased. Limit the adult dose to 200 mg/day. 62. Lidocaine: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor therapeutic concentrations if available. 63. Lumataperone: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dose to 5 mg/day if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 64. Maraviroc: Levels or effects are increased. Use caution and monitor. 65. Mavorixafor: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the daily dose with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 66. Methadone: Levels or effects are decreased due to CYP2B6 induction. Monitor for clinical response. 67. Methylprednisolone: Levels or effects are increased. Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids. 68. Mirvetuximab soravtansine: Levels or effects are increased. 69. Mometasone (inhaled): Levels or effects are increased. Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids. 70. Nelfinavir: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for adverse events. 71. Nevirapine: Levels or effects are increased. Use caution and monitor. 72. Nicardipine: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for side effects such as hypotension, flushing, and edema. Consider temporary dose reduction. 73. Nifedipine: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dose by 50% during coadministration and for 3 days after the last dose. 74. Norgestrel: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for adverse effects due to increased systemic concentrations. 75. Oxycodone: Levels or effects are increased. Monitor for therapeutic and adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. Reduce the dose if necessary. 76. Prednisone: Levels or effects are increased. Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids. 77. Quetiapine: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dose to one-sixth when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 78. Quizartinib: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dose to 4 mg/day when coadministered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Resume the original dose after discontinuation of the inhibitor for 5 half-lives. 79. Raltegavir: Levels or effects are decreased due to UGT1A1 induction. Use caution and monitor. 80. Rifabutin: Levels or effects are increased. Reduce the dose by at least 75% to 150 mg every other day or three times weekly. 81. Riociguat: Levels or effects are increased. Consider temporary dose reduction and monitor for hypotension. This list highlights the importance of careful monitoring and dose adjustments when coadministering nirmatrelvir/ritonavir with other medications.
